clue.text: Trail round Manchester with team making movie …

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to file is to walk along in a line, trailing one behind another
MCR is a common abbreviation for Manchester
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A crew trails around Manchester shooting a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only runs the surface into the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay. MCR is the common short form for Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who shoot a film together, camera operators, sound engineers and so on, form its crew.

clue.text: … taking case that contains new boom

indicators.note: something that contains another holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bag is a case for carrying things
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Continuing the film shoot, a case of equipment holds something that goes off with a boom.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis connects the surface to the previous clue only; this clue stands alone, with N put inside BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom and a bang are both loud sudden noises, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Requiring delicate fingering — like a violin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: needing nimble, careful handling
second, playful meaning: fiddle-like, since a violin is a fiddle

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a whimsical one: add -Y to FIDDLE and you get an adjective meaning resembling a fiddle; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Small awkward tasks needing nimble hands are described as fiddly, while a fiddle is simply an informal name for the violin.

clue.text: Old Satie composition is untypical

indicators.note: a composition is something put together or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Satie was a French composer

explanation.surface: A critic remarks that an early piece by the composer Erik Satie is unlike his usual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' reads naturally as a piece of music by Satie, but it signals the rearrangement; 'Old' joins the letters rather than shortening to O.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated case is a one-off, standing apart from the general pattern, hence unrepresentative or not typical.

clue.text: Hugest building by river is a bed and breakfast

indicators.note: building means constructing or assembling, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: The biggest building on the riverbank turns out to be a B&B.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugest building' reads as one noun phrase, but 'building' acts on the letters of 'Hugest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest house is a small private lodging offering rooms and breakfast, which is what a B&B is.

clue.text: Swallow rising over November landscape at last making dive

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
lying over something in a down entry can mean covering it on both sides, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to gulp is to swallow
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the final letter of landscape

explanation.surface: A swallow flying up over a late-autumn landscape suddenly swoops down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb, giving GULP, which flips to PLUG and takes N inside, before E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to jump or fall headlong into something, the same sudden downward movement as a dive.

clue.text: Dietary supplement's almost essential minimum with beginner to cooking

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: vital means essential
the first three letters of minimum, its usual short form

indicators.note: a beginner is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of cooking

explanation.surface: A nutrition tip: this supplement is close to the bare essential for anyone starting to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginner' looks like a novice cook in the surface, but it picks out a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascorbic acid, the nutrient found in citrus fruit, is commonly taken as tablets added to the diet.

clue.text: King died shielded by porter and nurse

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles

indicators.note: something shielded by another is protected all round by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A king's death is hidden by a hospital porter and nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' and 'nurse' look like hospital staff; the porter is the beer. CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles, as seen on royal ciphers.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a baby is to hold it protectively in your arms, which is the verb sense of cradle.

clue.text: Team's curtailed debuts in local league in gusty weather

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of local and league

explanation.surface: A team's first appearances in the local league are cut short by stormy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Team's' stands for 'is' and joins the pieces; 'debuts' is not about sporting firsts but first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust of wind, often bringing rain, so a spell of blustery conditions.

clue.text: Finally loses cup being complacent

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of loses
a mug is a kind of cup

explanation.surface: A complacent team finally gets knocked out of the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses' looks like the verb of the sporting story, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone pleased with themselves and too self-satisfied to see faults or risks.

clue.text: Omens not good after virulent gluttony and lust?

indicators.note: not good asks for the letter standing for good to be removed
after places one piece behind the other in the answer

parts.note: virulent means extremely harmful or deadly
omens are signs; dropping G, for good, gives the rest

explanation.surface: A warning that the signs look bad after an outbreak of greed and lechery.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNS minus G, the usual abbreviation for good, gives SINS, which comes after DEADLY. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony and lust are two of the seven deadly sins in Christian teaching, so the plural phrase defines them by example.

clue.text: Zen, surprisingly, stopping cook's mad behaviour

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug a gap in it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to fry is to cook

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Meditation, unexpectedly, calms a chef's wild kitchen tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on 'cook's' belongs to the surface only, and 'stopping' means plugging a gap rather than halting.
explanation.definitionFit: A frenzy is a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement or agitated activity, i.e. crazed conduct.

clue.text: Brown rat scuttled, occasionally so far, aboard barge

indicators.note: aboard means on board, inside a vessel, so one piece goes within another
to scuttle is to scurry about in a hurried disorderly way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of so far

explanation.surface: A brown rat that has so far stayed hidden scurries around on board a barge now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttled' suggests sinking a ship, which fits the barge, but here it means scurried, jumbling BROWN RAT; OA is then placed aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat is the long slim canal boat of Britain's waterways, essentially a type of barge.

clue.text: Lecturer at church has code which unlocks the door

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
a key is a code or cipher used to decode

explanation.surface: A lecturer at a church has the door code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' just joins the wordplay to the definition, which describes what the item does.
explanation.definitionFit: A latchkey is the key that opens the latch of a house's front entrance, so it is the thing that opens it.

clue.text: Swung off line and went round camper on bend

indicators.note: in an across clue, sitting on something places it after it

parts.note: an S-bend is a double bend shaped like the letter S

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to wee is to urinate, so weed is went in the slang sense of went to the toilet
an RV, recreational vehicle, is a camper van

explanation.surface: A driver veered out of lane and passed a camper van on a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went round' looks like overtaking, but 'went' is the childish sense of having a wee. RV, recreational vehicle, is the American term for a camper van. A tricky parse for a Quiptic.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to change direction suddenly, departing from a straight course, as a car does dodging an obstacle.

clue.text: Papers in flat about drug used to support testimony

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a flat surface is even
ID papers are identity documents
C is circa, Latin for about
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Documents found in an apartment, concerning narcotics, are produced in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is the apartment of the surface but means level here, and 'about' is circa rather than concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is material such as documents or exhibits brought into court to back up what witnesses say.

clue.text: Legal bill's going ahead with small changes

indicators.note: going ahead means coming first, so one piece leads the next

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD for short
just means lawful, legal
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill on law passes with only minor amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal bill' looks like one phrase, a law or a lawyer's invoice, but 'bill' is an advertisement that goes ahead of JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to modify or alter it slightly, so the verb is a synonym for changes in that sense.

clue.text: Young person born to be raised in great turmoil

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted to read bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
in places one piece inside another
turmoil is a state of confusion and disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
née, born, is used before a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A youngster born to be brought up amid great upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like the upbringing of the surface, but in a down clue it turns letters upside down; née is the French for born, used before maiden names.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent, a youth in the years just before adulthood.

clue.text: Heartily wished class was smaller

indicators.note: heartily is read as from the heart, so only the centre letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of wished
a rank is a class or grade

explanation.surface: A teacher fervently longed for a smaller class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartily' reads as an adverb of feeling but selects the centre of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrank is a past tense meaning became reduced in size, so a past form matching having become less big.

clue.text: Surprise: IOS hasn't worked

indicators.note: worked means shaped or manipulated, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; iOS is Apple's phone operating system

explanation.surface: A shocked user finds their phone's operating system has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't worked' reads as a software failure; 'worked' is the instruction acting on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to amaze or stun someone with something unexpected, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Deconstructing Proust produces lethargy

indicators.note: deconstructing means taking apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written; Proust was a French novelist

explanation.surface: Analysing the famously long-winded Proust leaves a reader drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deconstructing' is a literary-criticism term that fits the surface, but it simply signals rearranging the novelist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state of sluggishness and near-unconsciousness, close to torpor or listlessness.

clue.text: Cocaine's cut and ground

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
hewed means cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Drug talk: the cocaine has been cut with something and ground to powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' and 'ground' both sound like preparing drugs; the 's means has, joining C to HEWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground here is the past tense of grind, as teeth grind food, matching the verb sense of masticated.

clue.text: College student's constantly brilliant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for college
L is a learner, the crossword student
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: A college student is consistently outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone of high intelligence and quick wit, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Mixes up drink for fundraising event

parts.note: to jumble is to mix up
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone mixes up a drink for a charity do.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces run together and re-split as two different words. A jumble sale is a British sale of donated second-hand goods, often to raise money for a church or school.
explanation.definitionFit: Such sales of donated bric-a-brac are held by churches, schools and charities to raise money for a cause.

clue.text: Times and service reduced in festive season

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Opening times and church services are cut back over the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like hours of opening but is the multiplication sign; MASS drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is the informal written short form of Christmas, the December holiday period of celebration.

clue.text: Console cross and upset old boy with kiss

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down entry that turns the letters upside down

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone tries to comfort an angry, upset old man with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' and 'cross' look like the verb to comfort and the adjective angry; both shift sense. The Xbox is Microsoft's games console.
explanation.definitionFit: Microsoft's video games machine is a brand of console, so the brand name is an example of the device.

clue.text: Pieced together design in short time when back in charge

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A design was assembled quickly once its maker returned to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short time' suggests speed, but 'in' belongs with nothing: MO is the short time, then AS reversed, then IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture made by assembling small coloured tiles or fragments of stone or glass.

clue.text: Faint smell around pet's penetrating

indicators.note: something penetrating goes into another thing, so one piece sits inside
turning around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a reek is a strong smell
pet and love are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: A faint whiff around the dog has become rather pungent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faint smell' looks like one phrase, but 'Faint' is the definition. Pet and love are both British terms of endearment, as in 'all right, pet?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to collapse unconscious, and to keel over is the idiom for toppling to the ground suddenly.
